label: Overview
title: Wanderly is a trip planning platform that brings destination discovery, day by day itinerary building, and trip tracking into one connected experience.
lead: The goal was simple to state and hard to execute and let someone go from "I want to go to Italy" to a fully mapped, day by day plan without ever leaving the product or opening a spreadsheet.

blocks.label: This case study
blocks.text: This case study walks through the problem, the design decisions behind the core flows, and the system that ties them together.

blocks.alt: Wanderly home page on a laptop

label: The problem
title: Everything is disconnected, making trip planning feel complicated.
lead: Planning a trip often means using too many different tools one for inspiration, another for the itinerary, spreadsheets for the budget, maps for directions, and chats for coordinating with others.

items.title: Inspiration and planning are separate
items.text: Users struggle to turn travel ideas into an actual plan.

items.title: Itineraries lack context
items.text: Simple lists don’t show how places connect or whether the route is practical.

blocks.label: As a result
blocks.text: Users spend more time organizing their trip than enjoying the experience.

items: Make trip planning fast and easy.
Let users build trips step by step.
Show trips on a map so users can understand the route.
Give users one place to manage all their trips.

label: Design system
title: Plus Jakarta Sans
lead: Typography isn't just about style—it's about creating clarity, hierarchy, and effortless readability throughout every interaction.

label: Desktop view
title: From "I want to go to Italy" to a fully mapped, day by day plan.
lead: The core flows on desktop: discovering trips on the home page, creating a trip, adding itinerary items, planning each day on the map, managing trips and viewing trip details.
